rows.title: Local antimagic chromatic number of even-by-odd flower-bouquet graphs
rows.record_statement:
Let $r$ and $s$ be integers, with $r$ even and $r\ge 2$, and $s$ odd and $s\ge 3$. Let $rFB(s)$ denote the corresponding flower-bouquet graph, and let $\chi_{la}(G)$ be the local antimagic chromatic number of a graph $G$. **The even-by-odd flower-bouquet conjecture.**

$$
\chi_{la}(rFB(s))=3.
$$

The paper proves the analogous equality for odd $r,s\ge 3$, while the even-$r$, odd-$s$ case is posed as an open problem.
rows.source: Gee-Choon Lau, Wai Chee Shiu, M. Nalliah and K. Premalatha, “Construction of local antimagic 3-colorable graphs of fixed even size – matrix approach”, arXiv:2404.18049 (2024).
rows.what_was_proved: For every even r >= 2 and odd s >= 3 the graph rFB(s) has a local antimagic labeling with exactly three vertex sums, so its local antimagic chromatic number is 3 (each blade contains a triangle, so 3 is a lower bound). The source proved the odd-by-odd case and posed this one; its method is blocked for odd s by a parity obstruction in the column sums of its labeling matrix. The new ingredient is a 21-blade trade gadget, found by a role-aware exact-cover search, that rebalances the parity across blades; with it the source's matrix supply and grouping extend to all even r and odd s, with ten small exceptional cases settled by explicit tables. Lean defines the literal graph (hub adjacent to every blade vertex, the two path edges in each blade), labels 1..|E| with |E| computed from the graph, the colour count over all vertices, and the chromatic number as an infimum shown to be attained.

rows.title: The $q$-analog of the Markoff injectivity conjecture over balanced sequences
rows.record_statement:
Let $\mathcal{B}=\\{s\in\\{\mathtt{0},\mathtt{1}\\}^{\mathbb{Z}}:s\text{ is balanced}\\}$ be the set of all balanced bi-infinite binary sequences, and let

$$
\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{B})=\bigcup_{s\in\mathcal{B}}\mathcal{L}(s)
$$

be their language of finite factors. Let $\mu_q$ be the $q$-analog of the map assigning to a finite word $w$ the polynomial $\mu_q(w)_{12}\in\mathbb{Z}[q]$. **The $q$-analog of the Markoff injectivity conjecture over balanced sequences.** The map $w\mapsto\mu_q(w)_{12}$ from $\\{\mathtt{0},\mathtt{1}\\}^*$ to $\mathbb{Z}[q]$ is injective over $\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{B})$. This extends the $q$-analog from Christoffel words to the language of all balanced sequences, including periodic and Sturmian sequences; the supplied text gives no resolution.
rows.source: Sébastien Labbé and Mélodie Lapointe, “The q-analog of the Markoff injectivity conjecture over the language of a balanced sequence”, arXiv:2106.15886 (2021).
rows.what_was_proved: The polynomial μ_q(w)_{12} determines w among all finite factors of balanced bi-infinite binary sequences. The published tool, evaluation at a primitive sixth root of unity (Labbé, Lapointe and Steiner 2023, who proved injectivity on Christoffel words), recovers only the letter counts, and two balanced words from different sequences can have the same counts. The new step is the first derivative at that root: the two-letter commutator vanishes there, so the derivative is a function of two integer statistics recording where the ones sit. A second argument shows that a balanced word is the unique minimizer of a separable quadratic energy among words with its length and counts, so the length, the number of ones and the two statistics determine the word. Lean states the source's matrices, the left-to-right product and the (1,2) entry, balanced sequences on ℤ and their language, and checks the source's example polynomial, a pair of balanced words with equal counts lying in no common balanced sequence, and the known non-injective pair outside the language.

rows.title: Bruhn–Rautenbach's Fano-plane determinant conjecture
rows.record_statement:
Let $A\in\{0,1\}^{n\times n}$ have at most $3n$ non-zero entries. **Bruhn–Rautenbach's conjecture.** The determinant of $A$ is at most

$$
24^{n/7}.
$$

The bound is motivated by the incidence matrix of the Fano plane, whose determinant is $24$, and by disjoint unions of such matrices. The source presents this as an open problem.
rows.source: Igor Araujo, József Balogh and Yuzhou Wang, “Maximum determinant and permanent of sparse 0-1 matrices”, arXiv:2011.01892 (2020).
rows.what_was_proved: Every n×n 0-1 matrix with at most 3n ones satisfies |det A|^7 ≤ 24^n, so det A ≤ 24^(n/7), with equality for disjoint unions of Fano incidence matrices. The best published bounds were 2^(2n/3) (Araujo, Balogh and Wang) and 24^(n/6) (Scheinerman). The proof normalizes the matrix on both sides by its row and column degrees, bounds the logarithm of the determinant of the normalized Gram matrix through its trace and the trace of its square with degree-dependent centres (an integer-degree envelope that is sharp exactly at degree three), and closes with a linear edge/vertex potential that survives deletion of rows and columns of degree one; the induction runs on the potential bound, which needs no density hypothesis, so a deletion that raises the density is harmless. Lean proves the integer form |det A|^7 ≤ 24^n and derives the printed real-power form, and checks that the Fano matrix (21 ones, determinant 24) attains equality and that the hypotheses are satisfiable for every n.

rows.title: The eventual non-$\ell$-distance-balance conjecture for generalized Petersen graphs
rows.record_statement:
Let $GP(n,k)$ be the generalized Petersen graph, let $d$ denote graph distance, and let $D$ be its diameter. For an integer $k\geq 2$, define

$$
n_k=\begin{cases}11,&k=2,\\(k+1)^2,&k\text{ odd},\\k(k+2),&k\geq4\text{ even}.
\end{cases}
$$

**The eventual non-$\ell$-distance-balance conjecture.** For any $n>n_k$, the graph $GP(n,k)$ is not $\ell$-distance-balanced for any integer $\ell$ with $1\leq\ell<D$. Moreover, $n_k$ is the smallest integer with this property. The conjecture formalizes computational evidence that, for each fixed $k$, sufficiently large generalized Petersen graphs are diameter-distance-balanced but fail to be $\ell$-distance-balanced at every smaller distance.
rows.source: Stefko Miklavic and Primoz Sparl, “-distance-balanced graphs”, arXiv:1702.05257 (2017).
rows.what_was_proved: For every k ≥ 2 and n > n_k, GP(n,k) is connected and is not ℓ-distance-balanced for any 1 ≤ ℓ < D; at n = n_k some 1 ≤ ℓ < D is balanced, so n_k is the least threshold. Published work covers only k = 3, 4 (arXiv:2309.01900) and distance 1 with weaker distance-2 bounds (Ma, Wang and Klavžar, arXiv:2407.02635). The proof gives an explicit distance formula for GP(n,k) with n ≥ k(k+2), uses the rotation and reflection automorphisms to cancel the common layer-distance profiles of a pair at distance ℓ, and reduces |W_xy| − |W_yx| to sparse 'axis pulses' whose sum is shown to be nonzero for every 1 ≤ ℓ < D by explicit witnesses; k = 2 and the sharpness at n_k are handled by finite certificates and explicit balanced distances. Lean defines GP(n,k) on Bool × ZMod n with Mathlib's SimpleGraph, W_xy as the vertices strictly closer to x, and proves connectivity for all n > n_k so that the diameter condition cannot hold vacuously.

rows.title: The even zigzag-poset LE-symmetry conjecture
rows.record_statement:
For even $n$, let $Z_n$ be the poset on $n$ elements with relations

$$
v_1 < v_2 > v_3 < v_4 > \ldots > v_{n-3} < v_{n-2} > v_{n-1} < v_n.
$$

A poset is **LE-symmetric** when its Bender–Knuth group acts as the full symmetric group on its set of linear extensions. **The even zigzag-poset LE-symmetry conjecture.** The zigzag-poset $Z_n$ is LE-symmetric when $n$ is even. This is computationally verified for all even $n\leq 10$, while odd cases such as $Z_5$, $Z_7$, and $Z_9$ provide counterexamples; the even case remains open.
rows.source: Judy Hsin-Hui Chiang, Anh Trong Nam Hoang, Matthew Kendall, Ryan Lynch, Son Nguyen, Benjamin Przybocki and Janabel Xia, “Bender-Knuth involutions on linear extensions of posets”, arXiv:2302.12425 (2024).
rows.what_was_proved: For every even n the Bender–Knuth involutions generate the full symmetric group on the linear extensions of the zigzag poset Z_n (whose number is an Euler number: 5, 61, 1385, ...). The source verified n ≤ 10 by computer and proved only transitivity. The proof is an induction on n: removing the last two elements embeds the action for n − 2, and a commutator of moves supported on different blocks isolates a 3-cycle; the group is primitive because a block containing one fibre is forced to be everything, so Jordan's theorem gives the alternating group; finally the second Bender–Knuth move is an odd permutation, by a sign recurrence through the tail fibres. Lean defines Z_n literally (an even-indexed element is below its neighbours), linear extensions as position-to-vertex bijections respecting the order, the Bender–Knuth move as the swap of adjacent positions when the two elements are incomparable (proved equivalent to the literal rule), and checks the counts 5 and 61 so that the statement cannot hold by an empty or trivial set.

rows.title: The second q-analogue of Liu's Dwork congruence
rows.record_statement:
Let $m$ and $n$ be positive integers with $n\equiv1\;\allowbreak(\operatorname{mod}4)$ and $n>1$, and let $(a;q)_k$ denote the $q$-shifted factorial. **The q-analogue conjecture.**

$$
\sum_{k=0}^{mn-1}\frac{(1+q^{4k+1})(q^2;q^4)_k^3}{(1+q)(q^4;q^4)_k^3}q^k
\equiv \frac{[n]_{q^2}(q^3;q^4)_{(n-1)/2}}{(q^5;q^4)_{(n-1)/2}}q^{(1-n)/2}\sum_{k=0}^{m-1}\frac{(\frac12)_k^3}{k!^3}\;\allowbreak(\operatorname{mod}\Phi_n(q)^2).
$$

This is presented as a different q-analogue of the first case of Liu's supercongruence and as a refinement of an earlier congruence.
rows.source: Victor J. W. Guo, “Dwork-type q-congruences through the q-Lucas theorem”, arXiv:2310.15207 (2023).
rows.what_was_proved: The congruence holds for every m >= 1 and every n > 1 with n ≡ 1 (mod 4). Closest prior work: the block values in Guo's source, the base case from Guo and Zudilin (2020), and Guo's 2020 arbitrary-m result for n ≡ 3 (mod 4); the arbitrary-m statement modulo the square of the cyclotomic polynomial for n ≡ 1 (mod 4) was left open as Conjecture 6.2. The proof splits the left side into blocks of length n, shows that each block agrees with the right side's base value at every primitive n-th root of unity to first order (value and derivative), using a reciprocity under a shift of a parameter and a cancellation of the first-order shift errors between complementary blocks, and proves the base block by a terminating Dixon-type identity with an explicit WZ-style certificate. Lean works in the field of rational functions over Q with q the variable, states the congruence as coprimality of both denominators with Φ_n together with divisibility of the numerator of the difference by Φ_n^2, proves every denominator in the statement nonzero, and proves the base case rather than assuming it.

rows.title: Exact formula conjecture for the rainbow-saturation coefficient
rows.record_statement:
For each integer $k\geq 4$, let $f(k)$ be the auxiliary extremal function from the paper and let $\alpha_{k+2}$ be the coefficient in the asymptotic formula for rainbow saturation, so that $\operatorname{sat}(n,\mathcal{R}(K_{k+2}))=\alpha_{k+2}n+O(1)$. **Exact coefficient conjecture.** For every $k\geq 4$,

$$
\alpha_{k+2}=f(k)=k+\left\lceil\frac{-1+\sqrt{4k-3}}{2}\right\rceil.
$$

This conjecture is proposed as a way to close the gap between the lower and upper bounds for rainbow saturation by determining the auxiliary function $f(k)$ exactly. The supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.
rows.source: Debsoumya Chakraborti, Kevin Hendrey, Ben Lund and Casey Tompkins, “Rainbow saturation for complete graphs”, arXiv:2212.04640 (2024).
rows.what_was_proved: The conjectured formula fails: f(514) ≤ 536 < 537. Take three parts A, B, C of t vertices with every edge between different parts and none inside a part; add one private vertex for each triangle abc, put all private vertices in a clique joined to everything else, and give the edge ab and the edges from each c to its private vertex for (a, b, c) one shared colour, every other edge its own colour. A clique uses at most one vertex of C, so it meets each shared colour at most once, except the full triangle with its own private vertex; this gives a member of the source's class with t³ + 3t vertices for k = t³ + 2, which beats the formula from t = 8 on. A variable-core version gives f(k) ≤ k + 3⌈(k−2)^{1/3}⌉ for every k ≥ 4. Since the source's Lemma 3.3 proves α_{k+2} = f(k), the printed chain is false; together with the source's lower bound (its Lemma 3.10, quoted and not formalized), α_r − r = Θ(r^{1/3}), against the square-root growth the formula predicts. Lean states the source's three properties literally with colours in ℕ (the source's own palette), proves the refutation, the t-family, the every-k bound and that the formula fails for every t ≥ 8, and checks that f(k) ≥ k + 1 for k ≥ 1 and that the rainbow K_{k+1} is not a member.

rows.title: Growth conjecture for the number of orderings of congruence-class biases
rows.record_statement:
Let $\mathscr{O}(t)$ denote the number of possible orderings arising from the biases among congruence classes for $k$-indivisible partitions, and let $\varphi(t)$ be Euler's totient function. **Growth conjecture.** As $t\to\infty$, we have

$$
\frac{\mathscr{O}(t)}{\varphi(t)}=o(t)
$$

and

$$
\log t=o\left(\frac{\mathscr{O}(t)}{\varphi(t)}\right).
$$

Thus the normalized number of orderings is conjectured to grow sublinearly in $t$ and faster than logarithmically. The claim is motivated by numerical evidence and remains open.
rows.source: Faye Jackson and Misheel Otgonbayar, “Unexpected Biases between Congruence Classes for Parts in k-indivisible Partitions”, arXiv:2207.06365 (2022).
rows.what_was_proved: Both growth assertions hold. The orderings are determined by the second-order scores −ψ(r/t) + ψ(ρ(r)/t)/k of the source (ρ(r) the residue of k⁻¹r). The upper bound uses the source's own score formula: for each residue class of k the ordering changes only boundedly often before it settles, giving O(t) ≤ φ(t)(⌊t/H⌋ + 2H² + 2) for every H, hence o(t·φ(t)). The lower bound carries the new idea: for k = mt + q the label q is the unique label with the most right inversions, so the ordering reveals k mod t, and a counting argument forces a new ordering at every consecutive quotient m up to a power of t; Lean proves O(t)/φ(t) ≥ t^{1/4}/80 for large t (the written proof gives t^{1/3}). Lean defines ψ as Mathlib's digamma (with the series bridge proved), counts orderings over all k ≥ 2 coprime to t with no cap, and proves the statement for every relation family compatible with the score comparisons, which is how the source's Corollary 1.2 links its partition counts to the scores; the later no-ties theorem is not needed.

rows.title: A q-analogue of the Van Hamme–Sun supercongruence equivalence
rows.record_statement:
Let $n\equiv 1\pmod{4}$ be a positive integer. Define the $q$-integer $[m]=(1-q^m)/(1-q)$, the $q$-shifted factorial $(x;q)_k=(1-x)(1-xq)\cdots(1-xq^{k-1})$, and let $\Phi_n(q)$ denote the $n$-th cyclotomic polynomial. **q-analogue conjecture.**

$$
\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(-1)^k[6k+1]\frac{(q;q^2)_k^3}{(q^4;q^4)_k^3}q^{3k^2} \equiv \sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(-1)^k[8k+1]\frac{(q;q^4)_k^3}{(q^4;q^4)_k^3}q^{2k^2+k} \pmod{[n]\Phi_n(q)^3}.
$$

This is a proposed $q$-analogue of an equivalence between two supercongruences for primes congruent to $1$ modulo $4$; its validity for all positive integers $n\equiv1\pmod4$ remains open.
rows.source: Victor J. W. Guo and Chen Wang, “Refinements of Van Hamme's (E.2) and (F.2) supercongruences and two supercongruences by Swisher”, arXiv:2501.09626 (2025).
rows.what_was_proved: The congruence holds modulo [n]Φ_n(q)³ for every positive n ≡ 1 (mod 4). The proof finds a common finite q-WZ recurrence for the two sides under the parameter shift a → aq⁴, with matching boundary terms, which gives divisibility of the difference by Φ_n(q)⁴ at every primitive n-th root of unity, and treats the proper divisors d of n (whose Φ_d divide [n]) by a separate cancellation. Lean states the congruence as divisibility of the numerator of the reduced difference by [n]Φ_n(q)³ in ℚ[q], proves the only denominator in the statement nonzero, includes the review's required statement verbatim, and proves that the difference is not zero at n = 5.

rows.title: Vertex-cut obstruction for betweenness-uniform blow-ups
rows.record_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$ with diameter at least three and having a vertex cut of size one. For graphs $H_1,\dots,H_n$, let $G[H_1,\dots,H_n]$ be the corresponding blow-up of $G$.

**Vertex-cut obstruction.** There are no graphs $H_1,\dots,H_n$ such that $G[H_1,\dots,H_n]$ is betweenness-uniform.

This obstruction identifies a class of graphs that cannot be transformed into betweenness-uniform graphs by the blow-up construction. The supplied text does not provide a resolution status beyond stating the result as a conjecture candidate.
rows.source: David Hartman and Aneta Pokorná, “Constructions of betweenness-uniform graphs from trees”, arXiv:2105.06777 (2021).
rows.what_was_proved: The conjecture is false. Let G be the wedge of two 5-cycles (order 9, diameter 4, the common vertex a cut vertex). Replace the four neighbours of the cut vertex by K100, the four remaining vertices by K5, and the cut vertex by K604 ⊔ K8 ⊔ K4 ⊔ 25·K1. The resulting 1061-vertex blow-up is connected and every vertex has betweenness exactly 100. The source's obstruction for trees comes from leaves, whose parts carry no global load; in the two-C5 wedge every part lies on a cycle, and a part of the cut vertex that is a disjoint union of cliques adds load only to the neighbouring parts, so its number of non-adjacent pairs is a free parameter that balances the equations. The proof is a general formula for the betweenness of a blow-up whose parts are disjoint unions of cliques, from a lifting lemma for shortest paths; Lean proves the formula in general and evaluates it on the 9-vertex base, never enumerating the 1061 vertices. Lean's betweenness is the source's (unordered pairs), shared verbatim with the accepted 382260 packet.
